newsitem.title: UK: UK ITV head calls for cut in Treasury payments.
newsitem.headline: UK ITV head calls for cut in Treasury payments.

text.p: The chairman of the ITV Association called on Tuesday for a sharp reduction in the annual tender payments which ITV companies pay the British Treasury.
"If we are to continue to invest heavily in high quality original programmes, our current level of supertaxes need to be substantially reduced," said Leslie Hill, chairman of the ITV Association.

The 15 ITV companies pay the Treasury some 400 million pounds annually in licence or tender payments, which come on top of corporation tax. That sum consists of an annual fee plus a percentage of advertising and sponsorship revenue.

The annual fees vary wildly. For example, Carlton Communications Plc paid more than 46 million pounds last year for its London weekday licence but had to spend little more than 200,000 stg for Central, the English Midlands licence it also operates.

The ITV companies can apply to the Independent Television Commission (ITC) next year for fresh 10-year licences under new terms. They can opt to leave the licences to run until their 2003 expiry date.
Hill noted that the ITV companies faced increased competition from new terrestrial station Channel 5 and scores of planned digital channels.

"It is against this highly competitive background that over the course of the next 18 months the ITC will be considering the amount which a number of the ITV companies pay for their licences," Hill said in a statement.
"It is encouraging that the Commission has already indicated that it expects to see a reduction in the total amount ITV contributes to the Treasury in supertaxes."
Hill said he was "delighted" that ITV had maintained a 40 percent share in peaktime viewing in 1996, putting it six percentage points ahead of closest rival BBC1.

ITV spent 583 million pounds on networked programmes last year, plus 180 million for regional programmes. It is increasing its network budget to 600 million this year, with 200 million earmarked for the regions.
